sanskrit_verse:
आचार्यः शिक्षयेदेनं स्वगृहाद्दत्तभोजनम् ।
न चान्यत्कारयेत्कर्म पुत्रवच्चैनमाचरेत् ॥
transliteration: ācāryaḥ śikṣayed enaṃ svagṛhād dattabhojanam | na cānyat kārayet karma putravac cainam ācaret ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The Ācārya shall educate him with food provided from his own home; he shall not assign any other work, but treat him as a son.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of the Ācārya as foundational to consciousness transmission
Causation through direct sustenance and personal example
Capacity-based responsibility rooted in relational proximity
executable_legal_axioms: IF student resides under ācārya THEN ācārya provides sustenance directly from household
IF student is instructed THEN no external labor shall be imposed
IF student is taught THEN treatment must mirror that of biological heir
IF duty is assigned beyond teaching THEN action is invalid and non-binding
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes involving spiritual or educational lineage, the Supreme Court must recognize the ācārya's authority as ontologically prior to civil contract. The threshold of responsibility lies in the act of initiation itself, which establishes a familial bond. All obligations must reflect this elevated status, with restoration achieved by reasserting rightful placement within the ācārya's domain.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through the voluntary acceptance of instruction. Causality flows from the ācārya's decision to nourish and elevate. Responsibility arises only when capacity has been awakened. There is no punitive frame—misalignment dissolves upon recognition of the inherent relationship. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential awakening: first sustenance, then instruction, finally equality.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Re-establish daily sharing of meals until bond is reaffirmed
Responsibility assumption protocol: Ācārya publicly acknowledges breach if duties were neglected
Capacity restoration: Student undergoes purification and re-initiation if degraded
Integrity reintegration: Community witnesses ceremonial reaffirmation of son-like status
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores the eternal order between ācārya and disciple. Justice is executed through consciousness realignment alone. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
